::: {.callout-note title="Accepted behavior and delivery status"}
The backend, Route A/B lowering, handoff, Slurm execution, strict result
resolution and existing report summaries are part of the accepted V1 scope.
Recorded exercise evidence retains its limits; stabilization and release
delivery remain separate.
:::

## Public surface {#candidate-surface}

The public backend object is `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim`. Staged calls
expose geometry, terminals, solver configuration, mesh, config, handoff, and
result processing instead of hiding the workflow in one orchestration cell.

The intended visible sequence is:

```text
prepare shared GeometryPlan snapshot
-> set_plan (or fresh standalone geometry / stack / envelope)
-> add exact-net terminals and physical grounds
-> configure Electrostatic
-> mesh / config
-> common handoff
-> resolve / results / report
```

Handoff preparation does not submit Palace. Generated local or Slurm scripts
execute explicitly and write a receipt that the resolver verifies. Slurm
scripts bind `#SBATCH --output` and `--error` to `logs/palace-%j.log` so the
scheduler does not also write `slurm-%j.out`.

Before a generated script starts the solve, the exact copied `config.json` is
passed to the selected Palace executable with its native `--dry-run` option.
Only a successful dry-run of those exact bytes establishes config/runtime
compatibility. The compatibility artifact and returned receipt preserve the
config hash and observed native GitTag. When the configured executable is
directly and truthfully resolvable as the Palace binary, its basename and
SHA-256 are also retained. SCGSim does not inspect behind a wrapper to discover
its hidden binary. GitTag, commit, and any available binary hash are provenance
for reproducibility and diagnosis; their presence or value is not a
runtime-eligibility Gate.

If this preflight fails, the returned receipt records
`execution_stage="config_compatibility"`, `solver_invoked=false`, its separate
preflight and pipeline exit codes, and `solver_exit_code=null`. Receipts use
`execution_stage="solver"` only after the solver command was actually invoked.

| Stage | Public method | Intended responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Shared source | `set_plan` | Bind the immutable shared source snapshot. |
| Standalone geometry | `set_geometry` | Bind the public Component input to the SGB geometry route. |
| Stack input | `set_stack` | Bind the layer-stack input consumed by SGB. |
| Airbox | `set_airbox` | Declare the simulation-domain envelope before geometry production. |
| Terminal binding | `add_terminal` | Select a terminal by exact SGB net identity. |
| Physical Ground binding | `add_ground` | Select conductor components for Palace Ground by exact SGB net identity. |
| Problem controls | `set_electrostatic` | Declare Electrostatic-specific config controls. |
| Output identity | `set_output_dir` | Bind the mesh/config/handoff output location. |
| Surface films | `set_surface_epr` | Declare surface films and their inset margins; run it before `mesh()`. |
| Mesh controls | `set_mesh(...)` | Select the sizing recipe, mesher options, repair budgets and quality threshold. |
| Mesh | `mesh` | Build the SGB geometry, mesh it with `scgsim.meshing` and lower its groups to Palace attributes. |
| Config | `write_config` | Write the Palace Electrostatic configuration for the reviewed mesh identities. |

These methods are accepted public APIs.

Configuration setters are atomic with respect to this staged state. Airbox,
Surface EPR, and Eigenmode controls validate every supplied value before
changing any field. A validation failure therefore preserves the prior
configuration together with cached mesh, resolved-port, config, and handoff
state. A successful change retains the existing mesh/config invalidation
boundary; this does not change operational failures inside `mesh()` or
`write_config()`.

## Palace mesh controls {#palace-mesh-controls}

`mesh()` builds the geometry with SGB, meshes it with `scgsim.meshing` and
writes the Palace mesh, so the mesh controls are the controls of that module.
Both Palace facades accept them through `set_mesh(...)`, with the same defaults.
Omitted arguments retain their current settings. A change that alters a setting
invalidates the mesh, config and handoff; an invalid proposed value leaves the
prior state intact.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Control | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `recipe` | `FeatureRecipe()` | Chooses the initial element sizes: `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe` or `UniformBoundaryRecipe`. |
| `mesher` | `MesherOptions()` | Gmsh algorithms and the order of the delivered mesh: `algorithm_2d` (Gmsh's default when `None`), `algorithm_3d` (Delaunay), `geometry_order` (1) and `high_order_optimize` (`True`). |
| `budgets` | `Budgets()` | When the repair loop gives up: `max_rounds` (8 refinement rounds), `max_tetrahedra` (2,000,000) and a time limit of `time_limit_seconds` (180 s) for a model of at most `time_reference_area_mm2` (4 mm²) in x by y, growing in proportion above that area. The limit decides whether a round may start and how long its worker may run; writing the round's request and reading its result are not counted, so a result can arrive later than the limit by that much. `time_target_seconds` (60 s, scaled the same way) is reported, not enforced. |
| `quality_threshold` | `0.01` | The minimum signed inverse condition number (minSICN) every tetrahedron must reach. |
:::

Import `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe`, `UniformBoundaryRecipe`,
`MesherOptions`, `Budgets` and the `DELAUNAY` and `HXT` algorithm constants from
`scgsim.meshing`. The repair policy is not a Palace control: Palace always uses
the module's default `RepairPolicy`.

::: {.callout-important title="A mesh below the quality threshold stops the run"}
`mesh()` raises `scgsim.meshing.MeshRepairError`, carrying the quality report,
when the repair loop cannot bring every tetrahedron to `quality_threshold`
within `budgets`. It also raises when the mesh needs more than
`max_tetrahedra`, when the time limit is reached (a round still running is
stopped), when the count of bad elements has not fallen below its lowest for
two rounds in a row (`stalled`), when the accepted mesh cannot be raised to
`geometry_order`, or when Gmsh produces no mesh. No mesh path is returned, so
config and handoff preparation cannot continue. The report names the stop
reason, the time limit and the bad elements that remain; it is written to the
run's `mesh` folder, and the last mesh, if a round made one, stays there as a
`.rejected.msh` file.

When this happens, read where the remaining elements are. A stall usually
points at geometry the mesher cannot repair, such as an edge or a face one grid
step wide; fix it in the layout. Otherwise choose a recipe that sizes the
offending region finer, raise `Budgets.max_rounds` or the time limit, or lower
`quality_threshold` and record the lower value with the study.
`Budgets(max_rounds=0)` runs a recipe once without repair; it turns off repair
only, so a first mesh below the threshold is still rejected.
:::

### Sizing recipes {#palace-mesh-recipes}

A recipe decides only the initial element sizes. Repair, the threshold and the
report are the same for every recipe. Start with `FeatureRecipe`: it sizes the
curves the geometry itself calls for, and its defaults were measured to reach the
default threshold on 1 to 4 mm chips.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Recipe | Sizes | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `FeatureRecipe` | A coarse maximum size, the bounding-box diagonal over `max_size_divisor`, with finer elements at thin film sidewalls (a multiple of the film thickness when that is finer than half the coarse size). An optional rule sizes the outlines of the conductors. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1`, `film_sidewall_thickness_multiple=25`, `film_sidewall_ceiling_fraction=0.5`, `conductor_outline=False`, `conductor_edge_size_um=5`, `conductor_edge_grow_um=300` |
| `GlobalSizeRecipe` | Only the coarse maximum size, the bounding-box diagonal over `max_size_divisor`. A cheap reference that leaves near-flat tetrahedra at thin metal sidewalls, so it relies on repair rounds. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1` |
| `UniformBoundaryRecipe` | Every curve of the model at `near_um`, growing to `far_um` over `far_um` micrometres. It ignores what each curve is. | `near_um=5`, `far_um=300` |
:::

Each recipe has a name and a version, recorded with its parameters in the mesh
manifest, so a run states which sizing rules produced its mesh.

### Mesher options {#palace-mesh-mesher}

`MesherOptions` sets how Gmsh meshes whatever the sizes. Delaunay is the default
3D algorithm; `scgsim.meshing.HXT` is the alternative. Meshing runs on one
thread, and there are no thread controls.

`geometry_order` is the polynomial order of the delivered mesh, independent of
the finite-element order of `set_numerical(order=...)`. The audit, the threshold
and the repair loop always see the linear mesh. When `geometry_order` is above
1, the module raises the order of the mesh the loop accepted, optionally runs
Gmsh's `HighOrder` optimisation once (`high_order_optimize`), and writes that
mesh. A failure to fit curved elements raises an error; it is never replaced by
a straight or lower-order mesh.

## What `mesh()` writes {#palace-mesh-outputs}

The run folder holds the SGB model (`geometry/`, with the XAO and its sidecar),
the meshing report (`mesh/`, as JSON and text), `palace.msh` and the mesh
manifest (`metadata/`). `palace.msh` is a Gmsh MSH 2.2 ASCII file, the format
Palace reads. Palace lowers SGB's named groups to solver attributes from the
sidecar alone: it splits a surface group only where its faces are integrated by
different Surface-EPR rows or sides, so the attributes partition the faces and
nothing is counted twice. Electrical identity is the Net; the Terminal and
Ground bindings use the exact Net of the sidecar.

The meshing report states that minSICN and the count of tetrahedra below the
threshold were measured on the linear mesh before any elevation, and records
the order of the delivered mesh. To measure the stored solver mesh itself, use
the [mesh-quality reader](../mesh-quality.qmd).

## Mesh manifest and detached summary {#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary}

The mesh manifest (`schema_version` 2) records the route and its policy, the
sidecar schema and model identity digest, the Surface-EPR inset requests with
the band families they produced and the faces SGB skipped, the recipe (name,
version and parameters), repair policy, mesher options, budgets and threshold,
the path and SHA-256 of the quality report, and one entry per solver attribute
with the SGB group it came from. It also records the Gmsh version, node and
element types, physical-region element counts and edge-length statistics. Edge
lengths for high-order meshes are explicitly labeled as primary-corner chords
and reported in micrometres; they are not curved-edge arc lengths.

Both Palace facades and a resolved Palace run expose `mesh_summary()`. It returns
a detached value bound to the mesh and manifest identities. The Palace report
reads this same summary authority. Eigenmode includes an Nédélec topological
degree-of-freedom estimate based on primary-corner tetrahedron topology and the
configured FEM order. It is not an actual solver degree-of-freedom count;
changing FEM order updates the estimate without remeshing. Electrostatic's
H1 estimate is unavailable. The [mesh-quality reader](../mesh-quality.qmd) does
not calculate curved-element quality.

## Surface-EPR margins {#surface-epr-margins}

Surface-EPR inset margins are cut into the geometry as bands, so `set_surface_epr`
belongs before `mesh()`. The [Eigenmode contract](palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins)
owns the margin keys, the face kinds and the rows they produce, and Electrostatic
accepts the same specs. Calling `set_surface_epr` again invalidates the mesh,
config and handoff.

## Source and geometry authority

Read the [SGB geometry concept](../concepts/geometry.qmd#source-stage) for the
source-to-construction explanation. The contracts below define the supported
preparation paths.

Prefer `set_plan(snapshot)` for the shared source-first course. The standalone
`set_geometry(component)` / `set_stack(stack)` / explicit envelope APIs remain
supported on a fresh unbound simulation; do not mix them with a plan snapshot.
The [GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd) owns occurrence/Nets, generated
vacuum, contact and Route-A/B semantics. The current source-facing geometry
authority is `scgsim.geometry`. Palace builds its geometry with
`scgsim.geometry.sgb` (`build_sgb_geometry`) and meshes it with
`scgsim.meshing`. External SGB and gsim are derivation history only.

The [Electrostatic lesson](../course/palace-electrostatic.qmd) teaches exact Net
terminals/ground and the real mesh/config sequence. The separate
[Eigenmode contract](palace-eigenmode.qmd) defines mode and EPR output selection.
Neither preparation path starts Palace or submits a job. Shared private state
invalidation/persistence implementation lives in [architecture](../architecture.qmd#palace-preparation-lifecycle).

## Electrostatic defaults {#candidate-electrostatic-defaults}

These are accepted implementation defaults, not universal scientific
recommendations or adequacy Gates:

| Control | Default value |
|---|---|
| `save_fields` | `0` |
| `unassigned_conductor_policy` | `"ground"` |
| `exterior_boundary_policy` | `"none"` |
| `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal` | `false` unless the notebook sets `amr_nonconformal=True` |
| `Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptMesh` | omitted unless the notebook sets `save_adapt_mesh=True` or `False` |

Palace defaults `Nonconformal` to `true` when the key is omitted. SCGSim always
writes the key and defaults it to `false` (conformal tet AMR). Notebooks opt
into nonconformal AMR with `set_numerical(amr_nonconformal=True)`.

`set_numerical(save_adapt_mesh=...)` accepts only `True`, `False`, or `None`.
`None` (including omission) preserves the previous SCGSim numerical payload and
config bytes by omitting `SaveAdaptMesh`; a Boolean writes that exact Boolean to
`Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptMesh`. The control asks Palace whether to save its
final adapted mesh. It does not guarantee that a file is produced for every
solver run or private workflow.

`add_ground(net_id=...)` is the explicit physical-conductor path. It is
independent of `exterior_boundary_policy="ground"`, which adds the finite
solution-domain exterior faces. With `unassigned_conductor_policy="error"`,
every conductor component must be covered by exactly one Terminal or explicit
Ground binding. The index map records physical-Ground and exterior-Ground
attributes separately and their exact union must equal
`Boundaries.Ground.Attributes`. Existing
`exterior_boundary_policy="none"` plus
`unassigned_conductor_policy="ground"` remains the implicit-ground path.
Electrostatic authoring writes index-map schema v3, which carries the
physical-versus-exterior Ground split. The resolver reads only the current index
map and mesh manifest schemas; the
[report contract](../report-model.qmd#palace-run-schemas) states what happens to
a run folder of an older schema.

External gsim and historical SGB revisions are derivation evidence only. The
runtime geometry authority is the in-tree `scgsim.geometry.sgb` and the
current `scgsim.palace` implementation.

See [Geometry and SGB Route A/B](../geometry-sgb.qmd),
[Headless Geometry Preview](../geometry-preview.qmd),
[Execution Profiles and Local/Manual-HPC Handoff](../execution-profiles.qmd),
and [Provenance and Data Boundaries](../provenance.qmd) for the surrounding
contracts.
